newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's BCP to raise profitability '97.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's BCP to raise profitability '97.

text.p: Portugal's biggest private bank, Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP), expects to boost its profitability in 1997 by managing interest rate spreads on its products carefully, a board member said on Wednesday.

Asked if BCP would raise its financial margin in 1997, Antonio Rodrigues said: "We plan to carry on with measures we have taken this year to increase the margin and work on (interest rate) spreads both in credit and deposits."

He told Reuters Financial Television: "We have been managing very carefully the reductions in interest rates in Portugal...We have managed very carefully the spreads in both the mortgage business and the consumer business."

Rodrigues, who gave no results forecasts, was speaking a day after BCP, benefiting from a boost in consumer credit and insurance business, announced a 14.8 percent hike in 1996 net consolidated profit to 23.268 billion escudos ($140 million).
BCP's financial margin rose to 3.2 percent in 1996 from 2.9 percent in 1995.
Rodrigues said BCP would continue to raise dividends conservatively. "We plan to increase it (dividend payout) conservatively throughout the coming years," he said.
BCP's 1996 dividend payout was 41.1 percent, subject to the approval of the general assembly, up from 35.1 percent in 1995.
Rodrigues said he expected BCP's profitability to benefit from its plans to launch an "in-store" retail bank jointly with retailer Jeronimo Martins.
He said BCP's costs fell as it restructured following its 1995 merger with Banco Portugues do Atlantico.

"We feel now that particularly after the early retirement of over 1,000 employees of Atlantico, the results of the group will be affected by the reduction of the total costs, which we hope will be around five percent in 1997," he said.
He said the major objective of the merger with BPA had been to boost income by cross-selling to BPA's clients and by reducing costs via the early retirement programme.
BCP shares trading on Lisbon bourse ignored the 1996 results which were in line with expectations, dealers said.
BCP stood at 2,235 escudos, down eight, in volume of 64,415 shares in early afternoon trade.
